links.outcome: Discrimination and calibration of PREVENT on local Chinese cohort versus US validation
links.effect: AUC 0.61 (males) and 0.62 (females) vs US 0.757-0.794; calibration slopes 0.51 and 0.47; intercepts -0.79 and -0.54; marginal net benefit.
links.quote: However, ROC analysis demonstrated an AUC of 0.61 (95% CI 0.59-0.64) for CVD prediction in males and 0.62 (95% CI 0.60-0.64) in females, substantially lower than US validation performance (0.757-0.794).

links.outcome: Generalization of a US-developed risk model to a new (Chinese middle-aged and elderly) population
links.effect: Reduced discrimination (AUC 0.61-0.62) and poor calibration (slopes 0.47-0.51) in the Chinese population; authors advise extensive recalibration and further validation.
links.quote: Although the PREVENT scores were significantly associated with increased CVD risk, the equations exhibit reduced discrimination compared to US validation in CVD prediction among middle-aged and elderly Chinese individuals.

screen.reason: Retrospective external validation of the AHA PREVENT cardiovascular risk prediction equations in a Chinese cohort, assessing discrimination, calibration, and decision-curve analysis without testing a specific implementation safeguard or deployment practice.
